# external.tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments_by_day_historical

## Purpose
A **frozen, static GCS-Parquet archive** holding **11 days (2025-08-31 .. 2025-09-10)** of daily holdout IP-in-segment TPA (Third-Party Audience) membership — the same "which holdout IP is in which DS3 segment for which campaign on which day" fact as `aggregates.tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments`, but for the window *before* the live SQLMesh model's history begins. Its sole consumer is `aggregates.tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments__legacy`, which `UNION ALL`s this historical branch with the live physical (`date >= '2025-09-11'`) so full-history queries keep resolving. Reach for it only when you need those 11 pre-2025-09-11 days directly; for anything go-forward use the live SQLMesh `tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments` instead (partitioned + clustered, cheaper, richer types).

**Physical backing:** external federated PARQUET at `gs://mntn-data-archive-prod/static/tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments_by_day_historical/date=YYYY-MM-DD/*` (us-central1 bucket), hive-partitioned on `date` (CUSTOM mode). `bq show` reports `numRows: 0` / `numBytes: 0` — expected for an external table, not empty. GCS backing measured at **169.73 GiB** compressed across all 11 days (~14.45 GiB for date=2025-09-01). Actual row count = **16,449,116,829** across the 11 days (~1.4–1.5B rows/day; e.g. 2025-09-01 = 1,401,367,924).

## Grain & keys
- **Grain:** one row per **(date, ip, advertiser_id, campaign_id, segment_id)** — a holdout IP's membership in one DS3 segment for one campaign on one archived day. **Verified exact:** on adv 31297 / 2025-09-01, `COUNT(*) = COUNT(DISTINCT ip|advertiser_id|campaign_id|segment_id) = 244,146` (no duplicates). One IP recurs once per (campaign, segment) it is a holdout member of.
- **Key / join columns:** `ip` (join to event tables), `(advertiser_id, campaign_id)` (→ campaigns), `segment_id` (→ DS3 segment). `date` is the hive partition (a STRING here). No surrogate PK.

> Physical metadata: EXTERNAL hive-partitioned PARQUET, partition = `date` (STRING, from GCS path `date=YYYY-MM-DD`), **no clustering**, no TTL (static archive). `bq show` numRows/numBytes = 0 (federated GCS — expected). Partition confirmed from `externalDataConfiguration.hivePartitioningOptions.fields = ["date"]` and the `date=.../` GCS prefixes; a `--dry_run` cannot estimate cost here (returns "lower bound of 0 bytes").

## Column meanings (only the non-obvious ones)
- **`date`** — **STRING** in `YYYY-MM-DD` form (e.g. `"2025-09-01"`), the hive partition key, NOT a native `DATE`. Only 11 distinct values exist (2025-08-31, then 2025-09-01..2025-09-10). The `__legacy` consumer view casts this `STRING -> DATE`. No intra-day/timestamp precision — day grain only.
- **`tags`** — a raw **JSON STRING**, literally `["holdout"]` (JSON-escaped in output as `"[\"holdout\"]"`), **NOT** `ARRAY<STRING>`. Uniformly `["holdout"]` on every sampled day (1 distinct value) — every row is a holdout-group membership. The `__legacy` view parses this `STRING -> ARRAY<STRING>` via `JSON_VALUE_ARRAY`; consumers of the raw external table must string-match or JSON-parse it themselves.
- **`data_source_id`** — **uniformly NULL** in this external table (0 distinct values, 100% NULL on 2025-09-01). **DRIFT vs the live sibling**, where `data_source_id` is uniformly `3` = "MNTN Third Party". This frozen historical branch predates the column being populated; do NOT filter it expecting `= 3`. (The rows are still the DS3 holdout projection — the id is just absent in the archive.)
- **`score`** — graduated household / intent score, observed range **0–10000** (higher = stronger; note min is 0 here, a hair below the live table's stated 1–10000 floor). **NULL for ~41.7%** of rows on 2025-09-01 (584,916,710 / 1,401,367,924) — NULL = *unscored membership*, NOT zero. Do not `COALESCE(score, 0)` for averages.
- **`segment_id`** — the DS3 audience segment the IP is a member of (~12.2K distinct/day on 2025-09-01). No confirmed DS3-segment name dimension in BQ — treat as an opaque id.
- **`ip`** — holdout household IPv4 as a STRING; the join key to bid/impression/visit tables. Not deduped — recurs once per (campaign, segment) membership.

## Joins & relationships
- **Primary consumer — `aggregates.tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments__legacy`** (VIEW): this external table is that view's **historical `UNION ALL` branch** (rows where `date` in 2025-08-31..2025-09-10). **Row-preserving, 1:1** — the view passes each row through, casting `date STRING->DATE` and `tags STRING->ARRAY<STRING>`. The live branch (`date >= '2025-09-11'`) is disjoint by date, so no double-counting across the boundary. No fan-out.
- **`ip` → event tables** (`logdata.cost_impression_log`, `ui_visits`/`visits`, `bidder_bid_events`): partner side has **many rows per ip**, and this table *also* has many rows per ip (one per campaign×segment) → joining on `ip` alone is **M:N fan-out on both sides**. `SELECT DISTINCT ip` (or scope by advertiser/campaign/segment) before joining events. Mind the `ip` vs `ip_raw` convention on partner tables.
- **`(advertiser_id, campaign_id)` → `campaigns`** (bidder campaign / line-item id): **N:1** — this table has many rows per campaign. Roll up via `campaign_groups` if group grain is needed.
- **`segment_id` → DS3 segment metadata:** no confirmed DS3-segment name table in BQ (`tpa.categories` covers DS35/16/13/14/21, not DS3) — **live-unverifiable** this pass; treat `segment_id` as opaque.
- **Sibling variants (all in `aggregates`, VIEWs over SQLMesh physicals):** `tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments` (the live go-forward equivalent of THIS table, but native `DATE` + `ARRAY<STRING>` tags + `data_source_id = 3`), `tpa_membership_update_log_uber` (finer event log with `time`/`activity_time`/`version`), `tmul_holdout_segments` (related holdout roster).

## Gotchas
- **Raw untyped columns.** `date` is a STRING (not DATE) and `tags` is a JSON STRING (not ARRAY) — the opposite of the live sibling. Consumers must cast/parse (as the `__legacy` view does). Filtering `tags` needs `tags = '["holdout"]'` (string) or JSON parsing, not array functions.
- **`data_source_id` is 100% NULL here** (vs `3` in the live view) — the standout schema/data drift. Never use it to select the DS3 slice on this table.
- **Frozen 11-day archive only** (2025-08-31..2025-09-10) — never updated, never extended. For any date ≥ 2025-09-11 use the live `tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments`.
- **Holdout-only.** Every row is a holdout member (`tags = ["holdout"]`, 100%). Row/distinct-IP counts are the holdout slice, NOT total segment reach.
- **`score` NULL ~42%** = unscored, not 0; observed min is 0. Don't coalesce for averages.
- **No clustering — advertiser/campaign filters do NOT reduce bytes.** Unlike the live physical (clustered on `date, advertiser_id, campaign_id`), this external table only prunes on the `date` hive partition. A single-advertiser day scan reads the *whole* day's parquet (see Cost).
- **`--dry_run` is useless for cost** — federated external tables return "lower bound of 0 bytes"; the `bq_run.sh` wrapper's parser also errors on that 0-byte output (query still runs). Use GCS `du` or post-run job stats for real cost.
- **Severe `ip` fan-out** (~1.4–1.5B rows/day) — never join on `ip` unscoped.

## Cost & partitioning notes
- **ALWAYS `WHERE date = '<YYYY-MM-DD>'`** (STRING). The `date` hive partition is the ONLY pruning lever (prunes GCS objects); nothing else prunes.
- **Same-column-set prune (one INT column, actual bytes billed):**
  - `COUNT(advertiser_id)` **one day** (2025-09-01) = **11.21 GB** [actual].
  - `COUNT(advertiser_id)` **all 11 days** (no `date` filter) = **131.59 GB** [actual] — ~11.7× more, i.e. purely linear in days (no other pruning). = 16.45B rows × 8-byte INT.
- **Other reference figures (2025-09-01, labeled by exact column set, actual bytes billed):**
  - 5-col aggregate (`data_source_id, tags, score, advertiser_id, segment_id`) one day = **47.17 GB** [actual].
  - 4-col incl `ip` (`ip, advertiser_id, campaign_id, segment_id`) one day, filtered `advertiser_id = 31297` = **54.62 GB** [actual] — MORE than the 5-col scan despite the advertiser filter, because the filter does NOT prune (no clustering) and `ip` is a large STRING column. Proof that only `date` prunes.
  - `SELECT *` one day `--dry_run` = **"lower bound of 0 bytes"** (federated estimate is unusable).
- **GCS backing (compressed parquet):** 169.73 GiB total (11 days), ~14.45 GiB/day. BQ bills the *uncompressed* columns scanned, so per-day billed (e.g. 47 GB for 5 cols) exceeds the 14.45 GiB compressed object — a ~3–4× decompression factor. `approx_logical_bytes` left null (`bq show` reports 0; the GCS figure is compressed physical, not a BQ logical size).

## Example queries
```sql
-- Holdout IPs (with score) for one advertiser's campaigns on one archived day
-- NOTE: date is a STRING; advertiser_id does NOT prune (reads the whole day)
SELECT ip, campaign_id, segment_id, score
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments_by_day_historical`
WHERE date = '2025-09-01' AND advertiser_id = 31297;

-- DISTINCT holdout IPs for a segment (dedupe the campaign×segment fan-out before joining events)
SELECT DISTINCT ip
FROM `dw-main-bronze.external.tpa_membership_updates_log_insegments_by_day_historical`
WHERE date = '2025-09-01' AND segment_id = 428075;
```
